data.name: evaluation_description
data.value: Find every opportunity to make the meta and work-package workflows faster and cheaper to run. The primary lead is mechanisation: agent-executed technique prose that is in fact a deterministic procedure a script or server tool could compute without agent involvement — the worked example is resolving a named component, issue or PR to a repository and matching it against a monorepo component, treated as a guide rather than a boundary. In scope as subject: workflows/meta/** and workflows/work-package/**. In scope as mechanisation surface: src/** and scripts/**. Deliverable is a report enumerating opportunities, each with the saving it buys and what it costs to build.

data.name: scope_summary
data.value: Target /home/mike1/projects/dev/workflow-server, classified mixed. Subject: workflows/meta (5 activities, 150 techniques, 7 resources) and workflows/work-package (15 activities, 112 techniques, 37 resources). Mechanisation surface: src/ (712 KB TypeScript) and scripts/ (44 scripts, 26 check-* guards). Output to the session planning folder, verified writable. Five dimensions: Mechanisation Potential, Context Economy, Orchestration Topology, Redundant Work, Change Economics. Scoping-pass finding that shapes the dimensions: the server's entire tool surface is session control-plane with no domain-computation tool of any kind, so deterministic domain work in these workflows currently has nowhere to live except agent-executed prose. Confirmed by the user at the confirm-scope gate with option accept.

data.name: target_summary
data.value: workflow-server is a TypeScript MCP server serving 21 workflow definition trees written in markdown and YAML. The evaluation subject is two of them — meta (session lifecycle orchestrator, 5 activities) and work-package (15-activity engineering delivery workflow). src/ and scripts/ are in scope as the mechanisation surface. The server registers 16 MCP tools and every one is session control-plane, so deterministic domain work in these workflows currently has nowhere to live except agent-executed prose.

data.name: structure_inventory
data.value: workflows/meta: 171 files (160 md, 11 yaml), 290 KB, ~34,900 words — 5 activities, 150 technique files across 9 groups, 7 resources, 5 checkpoints. workflows/work-package: 168 files (152 md), 617 KB, ~66,300 words — 15 activities, 112 technique files across 16 groups, 37 resources, 44 checkpoints. src/: 12,343 LOC TypeScript (utils 4,000; tools 2,821; loaders 2,359; schema 1,621; transports 224; middleware 90; resources 66), 16 registered MCP tools (14 workflow, 2 resource). scripts/: 44 scripts, 15,257 LOC, 26 check-*.ts guards. tests/: 72 test files, 18,420 LOC.

data.name: key_topics
data.value: No domain-computation tool exists on the server. Checkpoint density is uneven — 10 gates in 01-start-work-package, 9 in 13-submit-for-review, 0 in 11-validate and 14-complete. Large bodies: dispatch-activity.md 10.0 KB, review-summary.md 9.6 KB, review-assumptions/reconcile.md 9.3 KB, review-mode.md 21.6 KB, codebase-comprehension.md 18.5 KB. Four technique basenames (analyze, create-pr, mark-ready, revise-session-metrics) exist in both trees, plus eleven parallel TECHNIQUE.md group files. The 26 check-*.ts guards are reachable only as repo CI, never as a workflow operation. record_usage and three benchmark scripts already instrument cost.

value.analysis_focus: The Mechanisation Potential focus, run through structural, adversarial and synthesis passes.
Each lens runs against its own dimension's focus and writes its own artifact within the shared subdirectory; the four foci are not merged into one prompt.

Evaluate the mechanisation potential of agent-executed technique prose in workflows/meta (150 technique files, ~34,900 words) and workflows/work-package (112 files, ~66,300 words): find every protocol step that is a deterministic procedure a script or server tool could compute. Use repo/component/issue/PR coordinate resolution (version-control::resolve-host-repo, monorepo component matching) as guide, not boundary; examine also path derivation, repo- and project-type detection, artifact link and anchor checking, sync-progress-status Progress-table writes, git and worktree state checks, classification steps that are fixed decision tables, and artifact format and schema validation. Judge each against the available surface: 16 registered MCP tools, all session control-plane, no domain-computation tool; 12,343 LOC in src/; 26 check-*.ts guards reachable only as CI. For each candidate, test whether the procedure is genuinely deterministic or whether the prose hides a judgement call.

Assess the context economy of definition delivery — tokens spent shipping technique and resource bodies into agent contexts. Measure body size against what a step actually reads: dispatch-activity.md 10.0 KB, workflow-engine/TECHNIQUE.md 8.3 KB, review-summary.md 9.6 KB, review-assumptions/reconcile.md 9.3 KB, review-mode.md 21.6 KB, codebase-comprehension.md 18.5 KB, against 290 KB of meta and 617 KB of work-package definitions. Examine the eager step-technique bundling budget, reference-versus-full delivery and the agent_id ledger in src/utils/delivery.ts and resource-delivery.ts, inherited-input blocks restated per technique, resources fetched but never read, and prose that restates what schemas/ already enforces. Name the abstraction that would collapse each duplication.

Analyse the orchestration topology of the two workflows — how work is distributed across agents and turns, and where the shape itself is the cost. work-package runs 15 activities carrying 44 checkpoint blocks across 13 of them, concentrated in 01-start-work-package (10) and 13-submit-for-review (9); meta runs 5 activities with 5 checkpoints, 3 of them in 00-discover-session. Examine dispatch granularity and the server-enforced batch bound (src/utils/batch.ts, dispatch.ts, fan-out.ts), worker round trips per activity (get_activity, get_technique, get_resource, yield and resume, record_usage), serial steps that could run concurrently, blocking-gate placement, context re-establishment at every activity boundary, and sub-agent spawn overhead. Propose alternative topologies and state what each trades.

Identify redundant work — steps the workflows perform that produce nothing the run consumes. Trace activities and techniques never reached in practice across meta's 5 activities and work-package's 15; artifacts written but never read downstream; verification repeated at multiple stages (26 check-*.ts guards alongside in-workflow verify-artifact-conforms, validate-workflow-yaml, validate-activities); optional branches that always resolve the same way. Examine duplication across the two trees, where analyze.md, create-pr.md, mark-ready.md and revise-session-metrics.md exist under both and eleven TECHNIQUE.md group files carry parallel structure. Distinguish genuinely dead paths from paths that are rare but load-bearing.

Evaluate the change economics of each optimisation opportunity — what building it costs and what it risks. For each, classify the implementation surface: a new server tool in src/tools/ (2,821 LOC, 16 tools today), a script under scripts/ (44 scripts, 15,257 LOC), or a definition edit in the 907 KB markdown and YAML corpus. Weigh the guard and test coverage protecting the change (72 test files, 18,420 LOC; 26 check-*.ts guards), saved-session and backwards compatibility for sessions holding the old shape, whether the saving is measurable with the record_usage instrumentation and the run-token-benchmark / run-dispatch-benchmark / run-batch-benchmark scripts already present, and sequencing dependencies between opportunities. Test the scarcity claims: which costs are immovable regardless of redesign.
